questions.scenario: Checkout has a business promise that 99.9% of POST /checkout requests succeed over 28 days. Which part is the SLI?

options.text: The measured proportion of successful POST /checkout requests.
The 99.9% target.
The 28-day review meeting.
The CloudWatch dashboard title.

questions.explanation: The SLI is the measured service behavior. The SLO applies a target and evaluation window to that indicator. Learn more in [CloudWatch SLOs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-ServiceLevelObjectives.html).

questions.scenario: A checkout service runs on autoscaled containers, so host utilization changes as capacity changes. The team wants a latency SLO that describes the user-facing operation and can drive an error budget. Which definition is most actionable?

options.text: Average CPU below 80%.
99% of POST /checkout requests complete within 500 ms over 28 days.
No application logs at ERROR.
Every instance remains running.

questions.explanation: A latency SLO should name the user-facing operation, threshold, success fraction, and evaluation period. Learn more in [CloudWatch SLOs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-ServiceLevelObjectives.html).

questions.scenario: A 99.9% availability SLO is exhausting its error budget rapidly after a release. What should the signal change operationally?

options.text: Continue risky releases because the monthly average may recover.
Delete the failed datapoints.
Use the burn evidence to slow or stop changes and prioritize reliability work.
Increase the SLO target to 100%.

questions.explanation: Error-budget consumption is a decision signal that connects reliability evidence to release risk. Learn more in [CloudWatch SLOs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-ServiceLevelObjectives.html).

questions.scenario: Checkout latency increased, and Application Signals shows a healthy checkout service but a slow payment dependency operation. What is the best next move?

options.text: Restart every checkout task without preserving evidence.
Raise the checkout latency SLO threshold.
Disable tracing.
Inspect the payment dependency operation and correlated telemetry.

questions.explanation: Application Signals exposes service operations and dependencies so the investigation can move to the slow hop. Learn more in [CloudWatch Application Signals](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Application-Signals.html).

questions.scenario: A checkout team is defining its first production reliability objective. Which choices produce a useful first SLO?

options.text: Choose a user-visible operation.
Use host uptime alone for every customer journey.
Define success or latency from measurable telemetry.
Use one host CPU metric as the customer-facing SLI.
Set a target and evaluation period.

questions.explanation: A useful SLO is tied to user-visible service behavior and has an explicit indicator, target, and period. Learn more in [CloudWatch SLOs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-ServiceLevelObjectives.html).
